:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x+5y &=5 \\ x-6y &=5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=
	\left[
	\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{array}
	\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -5 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-5y &=-5 \\ y &=-10,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-10$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-5(-10)=-5 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-8 \\ 2x+4y &=4.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 2 & 4 & 4\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 10 & 20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-8 \\ y &=2,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(2)=-8\,⇒\,x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=2.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+\frac{1}{3}y &=11 \\ 3x+\frac{1}{5}y &=9.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 3 & \frac{1}{5} & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & -\frac{4}{5} & -24\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{5}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{1}{3} & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 30\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=30$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=30.$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=
  \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & -8\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=0 \\ y &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+2(1)=0 
	\quad\Rightarrow\quad
	x=-2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\left<  -2,1 \right>.$

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Consider the following system of linear equations and its respective **augmented matrix**:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+6y &=-2 \\ 3x-y &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$
M =
	\left[
	\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{array}
	\right]
$$

If we can convert the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form, then we can solve the system using back substitution.

The procedure for reducing $M$ to row echelon form using elementary row operations is called **Gaussian elimination**. To perform Gaussian elimination on a $2 \times 2$ matrix, we use the following procedure.

**Step 1:** Consider the entry $a_{11}=2$ of the coefficient matrix. This entry is called a **pivot element**. We want to make this entry equal to $1$. So, the first elementary row operation will be 

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1
$$

and we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2:** Consider the entry $a_{21}=3$ below the first pivot element. We want to make this entry equal to $0$. So, the second elementary row operation will be 

$$
R_2 :=R_2+(-3)R_1
$$

and we have

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}1} & 3 & -1 \\ {\color{blue}3} & -1 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+({\color{blue}-3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}1} & 3 & -1 \\ {\color{blue}0} & -10 & 5\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3:** Finally, consider the entry $a_{22}=-10$. This entry is the second pivot element, and we would like to make it equal to $1$. So, the third elementary row operation will be 

$$
R_2 :=\dfrac{1}{-10}R_2
$$

and we get $M$ in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & {\color{red}-10} & 5\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{{\color{red}-10}}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & {\color{red}1} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=-1 \\ y &=-\frac{1}{2},\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+3 \left( -\dfrac{1}{2} \right) = -1 
	\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
	x=\dfrac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}.$ Or, in vector form, $\left< \dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{1}{2} \right>.$

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
The row echelon form of a matrix is *not* unique. In the previous example, after the first row operation we arrived at 

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}1} & 3 & -1 \\ {\color{blue}0} & {\color{red}-10} & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

This augmented matrix is already in row echelon form! However, it is always useful to do an extra step and obtain $1$'s along the main diagonal, like we did previously:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}1} & 3 & -1 \\ {\color{blue}0} & {\color{red}1} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

Having $1$'s along the main diagonal makes the final back substitution process a little easier.

	x=-55.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-55$ and $y=-10.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -55,-10 \rangle.$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 0x+2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
		1 & -2  \\
		0 & 2 
	\end{bmatrix}
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Coefficient Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}y+x-5-3z &=0 \\ z &=y+7x \\ y+3-2z &=1-2x\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-3z &=5 \\ -7x-y+z &=0 \\ 2x+y-2z &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
		1 & 1 & -3  \\
		-7 & -1 & 1  \\
                2 & 1 & -2 
	\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix  is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -3 & 5 \\ -7 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the Augmented Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What would be the system of equations for the following augmented matrix?

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}5 & -4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix consists of two parts: the coefficient matrix and the column of constants.

The coefficient matrix represents the coefficients in the linear system, while the column of constants represents the constants on the right-hand sides of the equations.

Using the variables $x$ and $y,$ then, the corresponding system of equations is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5x-4y &=-12 \\ 3x+y &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

:topic/knowledge-points.:knowledge-point/title: Finding the System of Equations Associated With an Augmented Matrix

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{c}{2} &=a \\ 5+3b-a &=4c \\ d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $a,b,c,d$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-a+0b+\frac{1}{2}c+0d &=0 \\ -a+3b-4c+0d &=-5 \\ 0a+0b+0c+d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
